premises.text: Conventional databases are rigid and force related application data into unrelated silos
premises.evidence_span: applications that had related data no longer were forced to store it into unrelated databases

premises.text: FluidDB is a shared writable database where any application can add any information to anything without permission
premises.evidence_span: any application could come along and add any information to anything

premises.text: Independent apps storing into the same place enable unanticipated combined queries across their data
premises.evidence_span: I've combined data in an unanticipated way from three independent but related applications

premises.text: FluidDB provides a shared writable object for everything—a platform for the web of things
premises.evidence_span: FluidDB gives you a shared, writable object for everything

value.text: Related information lives together so applications and people can add and combine data without asking permission
value.evidence_span: information that is related lives in the same place

secondary_value.text: A writable social future of data not owned solely by applications
secondary_value.evidence_span: The future of data is a writable future

causal_links.evidence_span: combining data from two different databases, is very difficult in the normal world
store their information into a place that makes it more valuable, because it's more useful

notes: Tickery/TunkRank/We Met At demos folded as cascade illustrating shared-store mechanism (§4.1.7). Funding/apartment bio excluded (§4.2). Writable-future vision recorded as secondary_value not a premise (§4.1.4).
